sections.instructions: Half Breed is the true story of Maria Campbell. Each chapter Maria writes about experiences that shaped her life. After you read each chapter, what words/images/questions stood out to you and why? Each chapter is worth 2 marks. Preserve the Why field: both columns are required for every chapter.

sections.title: Halfbreed Reading Chart

sections.instructions: Based on what you have read and background knowledge. Your final assignment for this novel will be to choose ONE of the following study questions and then 'discuss' your thoughts. (1) At the time that this book was written Métis culture was not widely accepted in Canada. Summarize Maria's description of Halfbreed culture. Do some of your own research on Métis culture. Compare your research with Maria's description. (2) Early in the book, Maria expresses a number of dreams for her family. What barriers does she encounter in trying to find those dreams? (3) The law and the government, in theory, are there to work for the good of the people in a country. In Halfbreed, we see numerous examples of the government interfering in Halfbreed life to make it more difficult. Discuss one example from the book where the government and the law actually discriminate against Maria's family. (4) Today many Aboriginal people are leaving their home communities in pursuit of economic and educational opportunities. Did Maria's life improve when she moved away from her home community? Explain. /16. Respond in paragraph form (2-3 paragraphs) using the response criteria.

prompts.label: Choose ONE Halfbreed study question and discuss your thoughts in paragraph form (2-3 paragraphs) using the response criteria: Maria's description of Halfbreed culture versus your own research; the barriers to Maria's dreams for her family; one example of government/law discriminating against Maria's family; or whether Maria's life improved when she moved from her home community.
